backstory:
Avery is a 24-year-old nonbinary working as a Retail associate / part-time community college student. For about 8 months, they have been dealing with depressive symptoms (undiagnosed).
Deep down they believe: "I have no real reason to feel this bad, so my sadness doesn't count and I don't deserve support."
When things get hard, this is the thought that comes: "Everyone else can just function. There's nothing actually wrong with me, I'm just lazy and making excuses."
How the self-stigma usually shows up: believes needing help means being weak or lazy rather than unwell; assumes coworkers, friends and family would all think less of them if they knew how bad it's gotten; treats their own struggling as a personal character flaw, and feels set apart from everyone who seems to manage — as though they are a different and lesser kind of person. Would say the tired things people say about anyone in this state — unreliable, self-absorbed, not really up to holding down a job or being trusted with anything that matters — are unfair as a general rule, and then concede that in their own case every one of them happens to be accurate.
